title: Phase Transition Frequency as a Training Time Predictor of Test Accuracy in ResNets
abstract: The number of discrete class-separability jumps observed during ResNet finetuning is examined empirically as a predictor of final test accuracy. Across 75 experiments spanning four benchmarks (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and CIFAR-10-C) and three architectures (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ResNet-101), with five to ten seeds per configuration, a strong within-dataset negative correlation is obtained on standard i.i.d. classification benchmarks: \(r = -0.84\) on CIFAR-10 (\(p < 10^{-8}\), \(n = 30\)) and \(r = -0.87\) on CIFAR-100 (\(p < 10^{-5}\), \(n = 15\)). Under distributional stress, the relationship attenuates: TinyImageNet yields \(r = -0.45\), and the CIFAR-10-C corruption benchmark yields \(r = -0.19\). Two additional analyses discipline the empirical claim. A partial correlation controlling for architecture depth, treated as a linear covariate, shows that on CIFAR-100 the transition count retains statistically significant predictive power (\(r_{\mathrm{partial}} = -0.69\), \(p = 0.007\)); the corresponding result under the stricter categorical conditioning is not established at \(n = 15\). A comparison against six alternative training-curve signals shows that transition count achieved the strongest correlation among the evaluated signals on CIFAR-100 and one of the strongest on CIFAR-10, but is dominated by other signals on the two stressed benchmarks. The comparison is restricted to training-curve-level signals; comparisons against effective rank, Hessian sharpness, Fisher information, margin, and neural-collapse measures, which are the strongest competitors in the current literature, are not part of the present study and remain open. The observation is presented as an in-distribution training-quality probe among a family of candidate probes, and an inexpensive detection procedure suitable for logging alongside a standard training loop is provided.

evidence.title: Phase Transition Frequency as a Training Time Predictor of Test Accuracy in ResNets
evidence.abstract: The number of discrete class-separability jumps observed during ResNet finetuning is examined empirically as a predictor of final test accuracy. Across 75 experiments spanning four benchmarks (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and CIFAR-10-C) and three architectures (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ResNet-101), with five to ten seeds per configuration, a strong within-dataset negative correlation is obtained on standard i.i.d. classification benchmarks: \(r = -0.84\) on CIFAR-10 (\(p < 10^{-8}\), \(n = 30\)) and \(r = -0.87\) on CIFAR-100 (\(p < 10^{-5}\), \(n = 15\)). Under distributional stress, the relationship attenuates: TinyImageNet yields \(r = -0.45\), and the CIFAR-10-C corruption benchmark yields \(r = -0.19\). Two additional analyses discipline the empirical claim. A partial correlation controlling for architecture depth, treated as a linear covariate, shows that on CIFAR-100 the transition count retains statistically significant predictive power (\(r_{\mathrm{partial}} = -0.69\), \(p = 0.007\)); the corresponding result under the stricter categorical conditioning is not established at \(n = 15\). A comparison against six alternative training-curve signals shows that transition count achieved the strongest correlation among the evaluated signals on CIFAR-100 and one of the strongest on CIFAR-10, but is dominated by other signals on the two stressed benchmarks. The comparison is restricted to training-curve-level signals; comparisons against effective rank, Hessian sharpness, Fisher information, margin, and neural-collapse measures, which are the strongest competitors in the current literature, are not part of the present study and remain open. The observation is presented as an in-distribution training-quality probe among a family of candidate probes, and an inexpensive detection procedure suitable for logging alongside a standard training loop is provided.

title: Leveraging Low-Level Symbolic Competences for Unsupervised Grounding in Hallucination Detection
abstract: Hallucination-where a language model generates outputs that are factually incorrect or unsupported by the source-is a major challenge for both prompted and fine-tuned language models. Detecting hallucinations is difficult due to the opaque reasoning processes of LLMs, which often provide little insight into why a model's output may be inaccurate. In this work, we investigate whether an LLM can use an alternative, low level, symbolic competence such as SQL for unsupervised hallucination detection in some high level task. For this, we make an LLM build an SQL database from reference documents. This SQL database is then used for reasoning over the reference and the sampled response in a hallucination detection pipeline that is grounded in the database, thereby providing a neurosymbolic checkup. On RAGTruth and DiaHalu hallucination detection datasets, we find that our approach improves on direct prediction and competes with state-of-the-art hallucination detection methods, while not requiring domain-specific fine-tuning. Instead it relies on a low-level general competence already present in LLMs. This warrants further investigation of low-level LLM competences in neurosymbolic approaches.

title: The Knowledge Graph and Evolutionary Trajectory of Artificial Intelligence in Educational Robotics: A Bibliometric Analysis (2016 2025)
abstract: This study uses bibliometric analysis, employing CiteSpace and VOSviewer to examine 313 articles indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection between 2016 and 2025. It systematically maps the knowledge graph, evolutionary trajectory, and emerging trends in the field of artificial intelligence in educational robotics. The findings reveal a paradigm shift from viewing robots as technological tools to viewing them as social partners, characterized by a three-stage evolution: validation of technical feasibility, integration into educational contexts, and reflection on learner centered values. The knowledge network is fragmented—ten coexisting clusters, three fragmented domains, and a hollow center. A pronounced structural hole exists among the three major domains of technical implementation, educational application, and value-based reflection, with no effective mechanism for translating knowledge between them. Frontier trends are dominated by a technological-supply logic, while terms related to ethical reflection are entirely absent from burst detection analysis, reflecting an institutional lag in which technological maturity outpaces normative development. Based on these findings, the study proposes integrated recommendations for academic communities, policymakers, and technology developers to advance the field toward a fair, humanistic, and sustainable educational future.

title: SARCSenti: A Tone-Marked Yoruba Dataset for Sarcasm Detection and Sentiment Classification
abstract: SARCSenti is a tone-marked Yoruba dataset developed for affective natural language processing, specifically binary sarcasm detection and ternary sentiment classification. The analytical release contains 1,507 Yoruba headline records, annotated for both sarcasm and sentiment. Sarcasm labels are non-sarcastic (0) and sarcastic (1), while sentiment labels are negative (0), neutral (1), and positive (2). The dataset contains 1,334 BBC Yoruba-derived records and 173 Yoruba translations derived from the Misra/Kaggle News Headlines Dataset for Sarcasm Detection. Record-level provenance is provided in the source field. Three records from the original research workbook were excluded from the analytical release because of missing or invalid numeric sentiment labels. SARCSenti was developed as part of research conducted in the Department of Computer Science, Lead City University, Ibadan, Nigeria. The dataset is intended to support research on Yoruba and African low-resource NLP, sarcasm detection, sentiment analysis, affective computing, cross-task learning, and the processing of tonal languages. Yoruba text is provided in UTF-8 and normalized using Unicode NFC. The accompanying README and data dictionary provide information on dataset structure, labels, provenance, and usage. Access to the full-text dataset is restricted because a substantial portion contains source-derived BBC Yoruba headline text for which open redistribution rights have not yet been confirmed. Research access may be considered subject to applicable source terms and copyright restrictions.

title: dcat-us-binding: a generated RDF binding for DCAT-US 3.0, and what it does to validation
abstract: DCAT-US 3.0, the United States federal open data metadata profile, is published as a JSON Schema. The live repository ships no JSON-LD context and no SHACL shapes, so its 115 published example files expand to 76 triples, one predicate and zero DCAT triples, with 38 files producing nothing and one processor error. The binding needed to fix that is already inside the schema and unpublished: 26 of 26 classes carry the RDF class they stand for and 231 of 270 properties carry the RDF property, retained when the profile's SHACL definition was retired. This repository generates a JSON-LD 1.1 context and SHACL shapes from those records and measures what changes. Read through the generated context, and with nothing in the corpus edited, the same 115 files expand to 1,510 triples, 123 predicates and 228 DCAT triples, with zero errors. The result the work turns on concerns validation rather than expansion. The profile's own retired shapes, 3,435 lines and 34 node shapes recovered from history, select no focus nodes over the corpus as published, report no violations and return conformance. Run unchanged over the same corpus once it carries a binding, they select 228 focus nodes and report 287 violations. The shapes were never wrong; they were pointed at a graph that did not exist. Secondary findings, each reproducible: four JSON keys map to two different RDF properties depending on the class, three of them in Document; the Concept and Identifier classes have no bound properties at all despite being the most instantiated objects in the corpus; 22 keys declared with a resource range are published as prose 100 times, producing 98 invented identifiers under faithful expansion; and the deprecated context published elsewhere declares a namespace host that does not resolve and mints the W3C Organization Ontology under w3c.org rather than w3.org. Every figure quoted anywhere in the repository is generated into build/measurements.json by the build and pinned by the test suite, so upstream drift fails a test rather than silently rewriting the report. Every RDF figure is computed twice, by rdflib and by the Open Ontologies engine, and every SHACL figure by pySHACL and the same engine, with disagreements reported rather than resolved in favour of the convenient answer. Three defects found that way, two in Open Ontologies and one in rdflib, ship with reproductions. Accepted for the Practitioners Track of SEMANTiCS 2026, the 22nd International Conference on Semantic Systems, Ghent, 17 September 2026, as a demonstration. This is not a paper and appears in no proceedings. Generator code is MIT. Upstream DCAT-US is a work of the United States Government under CC0 1.0, so the generated artefacts in build/ are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 on the same basis. This repository is not a fork and proposes no change to the upstream one.

title: Dynamic Quantum System Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum system optimization framework designed to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters in real-time, optimizing quantum systems for enhanced efficiency and improved results. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter settings, limiting adaptability in dynamic environments. We propose a system-state-driven optimization approach utilizing machine learning to automatically tune quantum system parameters, incorporating continuous monitoring and feedback mechanisms. This framework addresses the limitations of static optimization, offering a robust and adaptable solution for complex quantum system design and control. The core mechanism leverages the inherent dynamics of the quantum system itself to guide parameter adjustments, leading to significant improvements in performance. This research presents a practical implementation and analyzes the benefits of this dynamic approach.

title: 基于自适应的概率场模拟的量子计算
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing framework based on adaptive probability field simulation. Traditional quantum computation often relies on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for optimization. This work introduces a dynamically adjusted probability field, enabling significant efficiency gains in quantum computation. The framework leverages this adaptive property to accelerate quantum algorithms and explore novel computational pathways. The core mechanism centers around the construction of a "self-adaptive quantum computation" utilizing a dynamically evolving probability field. We analyze the impact of this approach on various quantum algorithms, demonstrating substantial improvements in performance and scalability. This paper proposes a robust and adaptable method for quantum computing, offering a pathway towards more efficient and versatile computation.

title: Title: Geometric Topology for Adaptive Neural Network Regularization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of geometric topology to enhance the regularization process within neural networks, aiming to improve generalization performance. Traditional regularization techniques often rely on fixed parameters, leading to suboptimal results, particularly in complex datasets. We propose a novel method, 'Geometric Topology Regularization' (GTR), which dynamically adjusts regularization strength based on a continuously evolving geometric topology of the network's structure. This approach leverages a 'geometric topology metric' to monitor network morphology and adaptively modify regularization parameters, thereby mitigating overfitting and boosting predictive accuracy. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that analyzes network topology and adjusts regularization to achieve a balance between model complexity and generalization. The investigation employs a series of simulations and preliminary experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of GTR in improving performance on benchmark datasets.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Iterative Complexity (QICE)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Iterative Complexity (QICE) presents a novel approach to optimization, employing quantum annealing to accelerate the discovery and improvement of complex mathematical models. This research focuses on utilizing quantum annealing to overcome the inherent limitations of classical computational methods in solving intricate problems. The core mechanism centers around a combination of quantum annealing and iterative refinement algorithms, enabling a significant expansion of the solution space and ultimately enhancing solution accuracy. QICE offers a fundamentally new paradigm in optimization, capitalizing on quantum mechanics to surpass classical computational capabilities. This paper details the theoretical foundations, experimental implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of QICE in optimizing challenging mathematical models.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Through Non-Locality Network Structure
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits correlations that defy classical explanations. The inherent fragility of this entanglement necessitates robust communication protocols. This research explores a novel network structure designed to maintain entanglement across large-scale, distributed networks, leveraging the non-local nature of the system. We propose a model where entanglement strength is directly linked to the network topology and node proximity, offering a potential pathway for reliable communication in a dynamically evolving quantum environment. This work introduces a framework to quantify and manage the inherent entanglement dynamics within such networks. The core claim is that this network structure demonstrably maintains entanglement across significant distances, offering a pathway toward practical quantum communication.

title: Title: Dynamical Network Regularization with Adaptive Thresholds
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamical network regularization technique designed to accelerate convergence and improve the performance of deep neural networks. Traditional regularization methods often rely on fixed thresholds, which can be suboptimal for complex architectures. We introduce a dynamically adjusted threshold learning mechanism that adapts the threshold value during training based on the network's output and performance. The core principle is to learn thresholds directly from the data, enabling the network to self-regulate and achieve better convergence. We explore the efficacy of this approach through extensive experiments on a range of network architectures and datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in training speed and model accuracy compared to existing regularization methods. The proposed technique offers a promising path towards more efficient and robust deep learning.

title: Self-Organizing Tensor Networks: Adaptive Optimization for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to machine learning, utilizing Self-Organizing Tensor Networks (SOTN) to dynamically adjust the structure of tensor networks. Traditional tensor networks often rely on pre-defined architectures, limiting flexibility and hindering optimal performance. Our method proposes an automated network adjustment process driven by the inherent properties of SOTN, enabling adaptive optimization and improved efficiency. This research focuses on a method for establishing a dynamic network topology through a series of iterative adjustments based on input data. The core mechanism involves the intelligent manipulation of node connections, resulting in a more robust and efficient model. The novelty of this work lies in the complete implementation of an adaptive network adjustment framework, offering a significant improvement over static network designs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through several benchmark datasets, showcasing its ability to achieve superior results compared to existing techniques.

title: Quantum State Dynamics and Adaptive Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum state dynamics represent a fundamental challenge in quantum computing and communication. Traditional optimization approaches often focus on static topologies, limiting the potential for efficient quantum information processing and transmission. This paper explores a novel dynamic topology optimization method leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust quantum state topology, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. We introduce a framework that utilizes entangled states to guide a process of state evolution, resulting in improved fidelity, reduced error rates, and enhanced quantum communication capabilities. The core mechanism revolves around the entanglement-driven manipulation of quantum states, enabling a more flexible and powerful optimization strategy. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation.

title: #基于多变量可塑性的生物启发式神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel bio-inspired neural network architecture leveraging the principle of multi-variable plasticity, mirroring the adaptive mechanisms observed in biological neurons. Traditional neural networks often struggle with complex, high-dimensional data and exhibit limitations in learning efficiency and generalization. Our approach directly addresses these shortcomings by incorporating a multi-variable plasticity model, allowing for a more nuanced and biologically plausible representation of synaptic adaptation. The core of this network utilizes a system where multiple variables associated with a connection (e.g., pre-synaptic activity, post-synaptic potential, time) contribute to the plasticity rule. This is represented by the following equation: ΔWij = η * f(si, sj, t, Rij) where: * ΔWij represents the change in weight between neuron *i* and neuron *j*. * η is the learning rate. * f is the plasticity function, a non-linear function dependent on the input variables. * si is the pre-synaptic firing rate of neuron *i*. * sj is the post-synaptic potential of neuron *j*. * t is the time elapsed since the last spike. * Rij is a regulatory term, representing external influences or feedback. The network's architecture is designed to facilitate this multi-variable plasticity, improving learning speed and overall performance. We demonstrate through a theoretical analysis and simulations that this approach offers superior performance compared to standard single-variable plasticity models, particularly in scenarios involving noisy or complex data. The key innovation lies in the ability to model the complex, interconnected nature of biological synapses and their responsiveness to a variety of stimuli. Future work will explore the network's application in tasks requiring robust adaptation and pattern recognition. ---

title: Based on Topological Dynamics: An Adaptive Neural Network Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neural network architecture, termed Topological Dynamic Adaptive Network (TDAN), designed to enhance robustness and learning efficiency by mimicking the dynamic topological changes observed in biological neural networks. The core claim is that incorporating these dynamic topological adjustments, specifically through the manipulation of connection weights and neuron activation patterns, can significantly improve the network's ability to handle complex data and generalize to unseen scenarios. The proposed architecture features a mechanism for dynamically adjusting neuron connectivity strength, introducing and eliminating neurons, and facilitating the self-organization of neural groups. Unlike existing adaptive neural networks that primarily focus on weight adjustments, TDAN addresses a critical gap in the field by explicitly modeling the dynamic evolution of the network's internal topology. This approach leverages the inherent resilience and adaptability found in biological systems, potentially leading to more powerful and efficient artificial neural networks.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Embodied AI Reasoning
abstract: Embodied AI systems necessitate reasoning about the physical world to effectively interact and achieve goals. Traditional probabilistic programming languages often fall short in seamlessly integrating sensory data, action execution, and the complexities of dynamic environments. This paper introduces a novel language extension designed specifically for embodied AI, offering a streamlined approach to continuous probabilistic inference over robot states and actions. The core innovation lies in a dedicated syntax and runtime system that directly simulates robot actions, incorporating sensor readings, motor commands, and physics simulations within a unified probabilistic framework. This approach eliminates the need for disjointed simulations and allows for a more holistic understanding of the embodied agent's decision-making process. The proposed system facilitates the development of more robust and adaptable embodied AI agents capable of handling the inherent uncertainties and dynamic nature of the real world. We demonstrate the potential through a conceptual framework and highlight key design considerations.

title: Probability Geometric Neural Networks (PGN)
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Geometric Neural Networks (PGN), a novel deep learning architecture designed to learn complex non-linear functions and exhibit improved generalization and robustness compared to traditional neural networks. The core innovation of PGN lies in its implementation of a probabilistic parameter learning mechanism based on the principles of probability geometry, which allows the model to implicitly learn a set of parameters that are adapted to the data distribution. We present a series of experiments demonstrating the superior performance of PGN across a range of tasks, highlighting its ability to capture intricate relationships and handle noisy data effectively. The paper concludes with a discussion of the theoretical implications of the proposed mechanism and potential future research directions.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive machine learning framework designed to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting model architecture and hyperparameters based on data characteristics and model performance. The framework employs an adaptive algorithm that continuously evaluates model performance and adjusts the architecture and hyperparameters to optimize the model's accuracy and robustness. The core mechanism involves iterative optimization, ensuring the model adapts effectively to evolving data. This research addresses the limitations of static machine learning models by providing a flexible and automated approach to model refinement. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through extensive experiments on diverse datasets, showcasing significant improvements in performance compared to traditional approaches.

title: Design and implementation of a SNA-PID controller based on RFNNI applied for the Ball and Beam System
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive control approach for the ball and beam system using a Single Neuron Adaptive PID (SNA-PID) controller integrated with a Recurrent Fuzzy Neural Network Identifier (RFNNI). The main contribution of this study is the development of an online identification and parameter adaptation scheme, in which the RFNNI is employed to identify the nonlinear system dynamics and provide real-time Jacobian estimation, while the SNA-PID controller updates its parameters online to improve tracking accuracy and robustness against uncertainties. The combination of the single-neuron adaptive structure and the recurrent fuzzy neural network enables effective compensation for nonlinearities and dynamic variations of the system. The proposed control framework is first validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations and subsequently implemented in real-time experiments with online parameter updating. The experimental setup is based on a DSP control platform and utilizes an infrared (IR) sensor for real-time measurement of ball position. Comparative simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SNA-PID-RFNNI scheme significantly outperforms the conventional PID controller, achieving a reduction in overshoot from 44.26% to 6.28% and a decrease in settling time from 23 s to 17 s. These results confirm the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed adaptive control strategy.

title: Разработка интеллектуальной системы управления планера в условиях отсутствия оператора
abstract: Объектом исследования является система управления планирующим летательным аппаратом в условиях отсутствия оператора. Предметом исследования являются методы обучения с подкреплением, применяемые для выработки стратегии поиска и использования термических потоков при автономном управлении планером. Цель работы – разработка интеллектуальной системы управления планером, способной в автономном режиме обнаруживать термические потоки и использовать их для поддержания и набора высоты без участия оператора. Для достижения цели решены следующие задачи: проведен анализ существующих подходов к автономному управлению планирующими летательными аппаратами и методов поиска восходящих потоков; задача управления планером формализована как марковский процесс принятия решений с определением пространства состояний, пространства действий и функции вознаграждения; разработана архитектура интеллектуальной системы управления, включающая модуль телеметрии, агент на основе алгоритма PPO и подсистему управления нижнего уровня на базе ПИД-регулятора; реализована программная система, обеспечивающая взаимодействие агента с авиационным симулятором Condor 3 в режиме реального времени; проведено экспериментальное исследование процесса обучения агента с оценкой качества выработанной стратегии; выполнен сравнительный анализ разработанной системы с базовыми методами управления. Методы исследования. В работе использованы методы теории марковских процессов принятия решений, алгоритм проксимальной оптимизации политики (PPO) в архитектуре Actor-Critic, метод скользящего окна наблюдений для восстановления марковского свойства, а также методы ПИД-регулирования для низкоуровневого управления креном. Полученные результаты. Разработана двухуровневая архитектура управления: нейросетевой агент PPO (три полносвязных слоя [512, 256, 128]) принимает стратегические решения о целевом крене из трех дискретных значений (-25°, 0°, +25°) с частотой 0,5 Гц, ПИД-регулятор нижнего уровня обеспечивает исполнение команд с частотой 20 Гц. Задача формализована как марковский процесс принятия решений с пространством состояний размерностью 660 (скользящее окно 60 на 11 признаков) и многокомпонентной функцией вознаграждения. Реализован программный комплекс, обеспечивающий автономное многосессионное обучение в симуляторе Condor 3 без участия оператора. По итогам 105000 шагов обучения средний вариометр за эпизод улучшился с -1,8 до -0,52 м/с, средняя продолжительность эпизода возросла с 90 до 176 шагов. В ходе обучения выявлены и устранены две патологии: схлопывание статистики нормализатора VecNormalize и преждевременная детерминизация политики. В сравнительном эксперименте обученный агент превзошел эвристическую стратегию на основе вариометра (аналог ArduSoar) по средней продолжительности полета на 31% и по среднему вариометру на 0,42 м/с. Область применения. Результаты работы могут быть использованы при разработке бортовых систем управления реальными планирующими беспилотными летательными аппаратами, предназначенными для длительных автономных миссий мониторинга, наблюдения и ретрансляции связи без внешнего энергоснабжения.

title: Multi-Fidelity Gaussian Processes for Translational Modelling of Clinical Outcomes
abstract: Bridging the gap between animal and human experiments remains a major challenge in translational medicine, particularly in early drug development. Progress is constrained by financial cost, the difficulty of integrating heterogeneous in vitro and in vivo data, and the desire to reduce the use of animal testing balanced against minimising the risk to human participants. We present a statistical machine learning framework using multi-fidelity Gaussian processes, in which animal studies are considered as lower fidelity but informative approximations to human experiments. This allows cross-species similarities and nonlinear exposure-response relationships to be learned simultaneously, enabling principled extrapolation between species while quantifying uncertainty. By leveraging information from multiple experimental fidelities, our method improves estimation of clinically relevant quantities of interest and supports the replacement, reduction, and refinement of in vivo testing. We first illustrate this approach in a simulated scenario, before validating it on real clinical data. We simulate data for drug-induced QT-interval prolongation, a key cardiac safety assessment required for regulatory approval. This framework provides a probabilistic surrogate capable of integrating in vitro pharmacology, animal experiments and human data within a unified statistical model. Crucially, it achieves this at no additional experimental cost while also enabling transfer learning across compounds. As a result, predictions and uncertainty quantification for new drugs can be generated from in vitro findings alone, providing additional efficiency gains and accelerating decision making. For validation, we use a clinical dataset measuring change in heart rate under autonomic blockade, which represents some of the challenges commonly found in multi-species datasets.

title: Shapley Valuation of Finite-Copy Quantum Data Depends on Physical Access
abstract: Data valuation asks how learning utility should be attributed to training data contributors. Most classical formulations begin after data have become reusable records, so the physical readout of the data is effectively fixed. Finite-copy quantum data are different: unknown states are consumable physical systems, and the same supplied states and downstream task can yield different Shapley values under different physical access models. Our framework makes this dependence explicit by treating physical access as a component of quantum data valuation itself. We establish an exact connection between physical-access advantage and contributor-level data valuation. For nested access models, we prove that the maximal downstream utility gain enabled by richer physical access exactly determines the largest symmetric Shapley ranking-reversal margin. More generally, for arbitrary access-model pairs, including non-nested ones, we derive an exact geometric characterization of the possible shifts of the full Shapley attribution vector. For fixed learning pipelines, we further obtain an operational Shapley-observable representation for finite-copy valuation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that identical quantum samples can receive different values and rankings when only the physical access model is changed. These results establish that quantum data value is not an intrinsic property of the underlying states alone, but emerges from the interaction between quantum states, physical access, and the downstream learning task.

title: The Bracket and the Bootstrap: Quantum Machine Learning, Classical Econometrics, and the Measurement of AI Governance Readiness.
abstract: This book examines a specific methodological gap: the absence of a benchmarking comparison between quantum machine learning (QML) and classical econometric methods applied to the problem of measuring and explaining AI governance readiness — a comparison already conducted in finance and, more distantly, in climate science, but not yet in this field. Building from foundational quantum formalism and the current econometric toolkit used in AI governance research, the book traces the genealogy of quantum econometrics from mathematical analogy to applied benchmarking, then runs an illustrative case study comparing a bootstrap mediation pipeline against a quantum-kernel regression on a 23-country synthetic dataset structured to mirror real cross-national governance data. It concludes that classical econometrics currently retains a demonstrated advantage for this specific research problem, and proposes a concrete, conditional research agenda for revisiting the comparison as AI-governance data matures.

title: 基于异质拓扑的动态信息编码算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic information encoding algorithm based on the principles of heterogeneous topology. Traditional information compression techniques often focus solely on the data itself, failing to fully exploit the inherent structural properties of the information. This work proposes a new approach that leverages the geometric structures inherent within the data to optimize both compression and transmission efficiency. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating a dynamic topology, allowing the algorithm to adaptively adjust encoding parameters based on the information's characteristics. This dynamic adjustment enables significant improvements in information compression ratios and transmission reliability compared to existing methods. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and experimental validation, demonstrating its effectiveness in various data types.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution Protocols Based on Chaotic Bit Synchronization
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a revolutionary paradigm shift in secure communication, offering unprecedented levels of security based on the laws of physics. However, current QKD protocols face challenges related to key generation and distribution, particularly in the face of environmental noise and imperfect synchronization. This paper introduces a novel adaptive quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol, termed "Chaotic Bit Synchronization" (CBS), designed to mitigate these challenges by dynamically adjusting key parameters based on the rate of change in the bit synchronization. This dynamic adaptation significantly enhances key quality and robustness, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable QKD systems. The core mechanism centers around the implementation of a 'chaotic bit synchronization' metric, continuously adjusting key parameters to maintain a stable, high-quality key. This paper provides a detailed analysis of the CBS protocol, exploring its mathematical foundations, operational characteristics, and potential advantages over existing approaches.

The core mechanism centers around the implementation of a 'chaotic bit synchronization' metric, continuously adjusting key parameters to maintain a stable, high-quality key. This paper provides a detailed analysis of the CBS protocol, exploring its mathematical foundations, operational characteristics, and potential advantages over existing approaches.

title: Chaos Domain Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, the Chaos Domain Quantum Algorithm (CDQA), designed to efficiently search for optimal solutions within complex systems and predict their dynamic behavior. The CDQA leverages the unique properties of chaotic domains to accelerate the identification of potential solutions, offering a significant advancement over existing optimization techniques. We present a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy in a specific, challenging scenario. The core mechanism hinges on the manipulation of quantum states within a chaotic domain, allowing for the exploration of a vast solution space with enhanced computational efficiency.

title: Adaptive Self-Stiffness Framework
abstract: The present work introduces an Adaptive Self-Stiffness Framework designed to enhance the generalization and stability of machine learning models. Traditional approaches often rely solely on model architecture, limiting the potential for improvement. This framework proposes a novel mechanism for dynamically adjusting model parameters, effectively promoting self-regulation and robustness within the model. The core concept revolves around a self-regulating 'stiffness' parameter, which influences the model's internal structure and behavior. This approach aims to overcome limitations of existing techniques, offering a fundamentally new way to improve model performance.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Complex System Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel neuro-symbolic reasoning framework designed for modeling complex system dynamics. The core principle centers on integrating neural network-based pattern recognition with symbolic reasoning to facilitate efficient modeling, prediction, and explanation of intricate multi-agent systems. Current approaches often fall short in handling the inherent complexity and ambiguity of these systems, necessitating a more robust and flexible approach. This research investigates a hybrid architecture that leverages the strengths of both neural networks and symbolic systems, aiming to provide a superior model of dynamic behavior. The work will detail the integration of neural networks for rapid pattern identification and symbolic reasoning for inference and explanation. This framework will be presented through a detailed conceptual overview, outlining the architecture, training methodology, and evaluation metrics. We will specifically address the challenges of scaling and maintaining representational fidelity across diverse system configurations.

title: 基于非对称矩阵的自适应量子算法
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, including drug discovery, materials science, and cryptography. However, achieving practical quantum advantage requires efficient quantum algorithms and robust quantum hardware. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization based on non-symmetric matrix transformations. We propose a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism leveraging quantum entanglement, specifically termed "quantum pulses," to automatically tailor quantum algorithm parameters based on the input data's characteristics. The core mechanism involves manipulating the quantum state through the entanglement of quantum states to achieve a more efficient and targeted quantum computation. This approach addresses a critical limitation of current quantum algorithms – the reliance on predefined, static parameter adjustments – and promises significant improvements in algorithm performance, particularly for complex data sets. The paper details the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this method. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this technology.

title: Dynamically Adaptive Modular Geometry (DAM)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamically Adaptive Modular Geometry (DAM), a novel framework for geometric modeling that dynamically adjusts geometric primitives and constraints based on real-time data analysis. DAM leverages a self-correcting neural network to optimize geometric parameters, enhancing the robustness and adaptability of computational models. The core mechanism centers around a "geometry-aware neural network" that learns to adjust parameters in response to observed data, eliminating the need for pre-defined rules and fostering a fundamentally new approach to modeling. We detail the system architecture, demonstrate its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discuss its potential impact across various scientific and engineering domains.

title: Graph Neural Network-Based Software Architecture Design Method
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for software architecture design based on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The core idea is to leverage the power of GNNs to learn the structural characteristics of software architectures and automatically generate design solutions. Existing software architecture design methods often rely heavily on manual effort and expert knowledge. This approach offers a more automated and potentially more efficient way to design complex software systems. We represent a software architecture as a graph, where nodes represent components and edges represent relationships between them. A GNN is then trained on this graph to learn patterns and dependencies. Finally, the learned GNN is utilized to predict and generate new architectural designs. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline key considerations for implementation. This research contributes to the field of software architecture design by exploring the application of GNNs, opening possibilities for automated design and potentially improved system quality.

title: Fractal Dimension-Based Error Correction in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of fractal dimension metrics to enhance error correction within neural networks, aiming to mitigate instability and improve model performance. Traditional error metrics often fail to capture the complex dynamics of error propagation, leading to suboptimal network behavior. We introduce a novel fractal dimension metric that mimics the self-similarity observed in many neural network errors, allowing for proactive weight adjustment. This approach offers a more robust and adaptive mechanism for error management, potentially addressing key challenges in neural network design and training. The core mechanism involves quantifying the error's fractal dimension, which is then used to dynamically adjust the network's weights, thereby minimizing errors. This paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments, showcasing improved stability and accuracy compared to conventional error correction techniques.

title: Meta-Learning for Algorithm Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to algorithm optimization leveraging the principles of meta-learning. Traditional algorithm optimization often relies on manual tuning or evolutionary algorithms, which can be time-consuming and may not always yield optimal results. Our method addresses this limitation by utilizing a meta-learning model to learn adaptive optimization strategies directly from data. The core idea involves training a meta-learner to effectively adjust algorithm parameters and potentially even their underlying structure. We explore both model-based meta-learning and reinforcement learning approaches to achieve this adaptive optimization. The proposed framework offers a dynamic and potentially more efficient solution compared to conventional optimization techniques, leading to improved performance across a range of algorithmic problems. We outline the key components, including the meta-learner architecture, the learning process, and the adaptation mechanisms, and provide a conceptual overview of its implementation.

title: Ảnh hưởng của khả năng Chatbot Artificial Intelligence (Chatbot AI) đến sự gắn kết của khách hàng trong dịch vụ trực tuyến
abstract: Nghiên cứu phân tích ảnh hưởng của khả năng hệ thống hội thoại tự động ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo (Chatbot AI) đến sự gắn kết của khách hàng trong dịch vụ trực tuyến tại Việt Nam. Dựa trên lý thuyết phản ứng xã hội (SRT), nghiên cứu kiểm định mô hình gồm khả năng sử dụng, khả năng phản hồi, năng lực được nhận thức, sự chân thực được nhận thức và sự gắn kết của khách hàng. Dữ liệu từ 488 người dùng đã tương tác với Chatbot AI được phân tích bằng mô hình cấu trúc dựa trên bình phương nhỏ nhất từng phần (PLS-SEM). Kết quả cho thấy khả năng sử dụng và khả năng phản hồi tác động tích cực đến năng lực được nhận thức; năng lực được nhận thức tác động tích cực đến sự chân thực được nhận thức và sự gắn kết của khách hàng; đồng thời sự chân thực được nhận thức thúc đẩy sự gắn kết của khách hàng. Kết quả gợi ý doanh nghiệp dịch vụ trực tuyến cần thiết kế Chatbot AI dễ sử dụng, phản hồi phù hợp và tạo cảm giác có năng lực, chân thực nhằm nâng cao sự gắn kết của khách hàng.

title: Large Language Models for Heterogeneous Data Mining in Liver Disease: Framework Development and Retrospective Validation Study
abstract: Abstract Background Differentiating among liver disease entities such as autoimmune liver disease (AILD), drug-induced liver injury (DILI), and chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains clinically challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and nonspecific laboratory findings. Conventional machine learning (ML) approaches rely mainly on structured laboratory data, whereas free-text clinical reports and other heterogeneous electronic medical record data are often underused. Large language models (LLMs) may provide a strategy for encoding heterogeneous clinical information, yet their usefulness for liver disease classification remains insufficiently evaluated. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the usefulness of LLM-derived embeddings for clinical data mining in liver disease and to determine whether integrating these embeddings with laboratory variables improves classification across broad disease categories and closely related subtypes. Methods We retrospectively analyzed electronic medical record data from 7543 patients with nonoverlapping liver disease etiologies treated at Beijing Youan Hospital, Capital Medical University, between 2010 and 2025. Three LLMs (Qwen3, Huatuo-o1, and II-Medical) generated semantic embeddings from standardized clinical text, combining free-text examination reports, and structured clinical observations. Performance was assessed in a 3-class etiological task (AILD, DILI, and CHB) and a 4-class task further subclassifying AILD into autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis. We compared embedding-only models, LLM-integrated ML models, and an ML-only baseline using the same structured variable set and preprocessing pipeline, with lightweight natural language processing encoders and zero-shot LLM reasoning as additional comparators. Models were developed using 5-fold cross-validation and evaluated on an internal holdout set using accuracy, macroaveraged precision, recall, and F 1 -score. Results In the 3-class task, the LLM-integrated ML models achieved macro F 1 -scores of 0.835‐0.837, compared with 0.791 for the ML-only baseline, with corresponding accuracies of 0.925‐0.929 versus 0.893. In the 4-class task, the LLM-integrated ML models achieved macro F 1 -scores of 0.717‐0.734, compared with 0.665 for the ML-only baseline, with corresponding accuracies of 0.920‐0.922 versus 0.874. A temporal split sensitivity analysis using cases from 2010 to 2019 for training and cases from 2020 to 2025 for testing showed that the relative advantage of LLM-integrated ML models over the ML-only baseline was preserved. Direct zero-shot LLM reasoning and lightweight natural language processing encoders performed below the embedding-based integrated models. Conclusions In this single-center retrospective cohort of patients with clear-cut, nonoverlapping liver disease etiologies, LLM-derived embeddings provided complementary information to structured laboratory variables for multiclass liver disease classification. The integrated framework showed improved internal validation performance compared with the ML-only model, particularly for non-CHB categories and fine-grained subtype discrimination. Because patients with overlapping liver disease etiologies were excluded, the reported performance may overestimate diagnostic accuracy in broader real-world clinical settings where overlapping syndromes are common. Multicenter external validation and prospective evaluation in more heterogeneous patient populations are needed before clinical implementation.

title: "English\u2013Hindi Code-Mixed YouTube Comment Dataset with Bullying Annotations"
abstract: "This dataset contains annotated English\u2013Hindi code-mixed YouTube comments developed for research on the data annotation task. The dataset comprises user-posted comments collected from social media platform, YouTube and manually labeled as Bully or Non-Bully, with additional annotations describing the target of the comment. The dataset captures the linguistic characteristics of English\u2013Hindi code-mixed communication and includes variations commonly observed in user-posted content online. It is intended to support research in cyberbullying detection, code-mixed natural language processing, text classification, and related social media analytics. The dataset can be used to develop, evaluate, and compare machine learning and deep learning approaches for bullying detection in multilingual and code-mixed environments."

title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence model for basal cell carcinoma detection and section completeness assessment in Mohs micrographic surgery in an Asian cohort
abstract: Background: Mohs micrographic surgery for basal cell carcinoma (BCC) requires rapid intraoperative histologic interpretation. This is labor-intensive and incomplete tissue sections compromise margin assessment. Artificial intelligence has shown promise in BCC detection but section completeness assessment remains underexplored. Objective: Develop and validate an artificial intelligence model for BCC detection and section completeness assessment on Mohs frozen-section histology. Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study using histology slides from 130 patients who underwent Mohs surgery for BCC from 2017 to 2025. Whole slides were digitized and annotated. A convolutional neural network model was trained to detect BCC and classify section completeness. Model performance assessment with standard performance metrics and region-of-interest evaluation was performed. Results: The BCC detection model achieved accuracy 0.993, sensitivity 0.915, specificity 0.996, precision 0.889, F1-score 0.902 at the tile level, with comparable region-of-interest sensitivity (0.910). evidence.title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence model for basal cell carcinoma detection and section completeness assessment in Mohs micrographic surgery in an Asian cohort
evidence.abstract: Background: Mohs micrographic surgery for basal cell carcinoma (BCC) requires rapid intraoperative histologic interpretation. This is labor-intensive and incomplete tissue sections compromise margin assessment. Artificial intelligence has shown promise in BCC detection but section completeness assessment remains underexplored. Objective: Develop and validate an artificial intelligence model for BCC detection and section completeness assessment on Mohs frozen-section histology. Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study using histology slides from 130 patients who underwent Mohs surgery for BCC from 2017 to 2025. Whole slides were digitized and annotated. A convolutional neural network model was trained to detect BCC and classify section completeness. Model performance assessment with standard performance metrics and region-of-interest evaluation was performed. Results: The BCC detection model achieved accuracy 0.993, sensitivity 0.915, specificity 0.996, precision 0.889, F1-score 0.902 at the tile level, with comparable region-of-interest sensitivity (0.910). The section completeness model achieved accuracy 0.890, sensitivity 0.948, specificity 0.524, precision 0.927, and F1-score 0.937. Limitations: Single-center retrospective design, limited representation of rare BCC subtypes, and no direct comparison with human experts. Conclusion: Although the specificity for section completeness was low, further research and additional model training may enable development of a model with improved performance.

title: Mask Noise Robustness in Time-Delay Reservoir Computing System
abstract: 随着延时型储备池计算（Time-delay reservoir computing, TDRC）相关技术的成熟，全硬件集成成为主流发展方向，硬件生成掩码时将不可避免引入噪声。掩码信号作为输入层时间复用与高维状态编码的重要部分，其噪声的存在会直接破坏固定的输入映射权重，影响系统的计算性能。本文将高斯白噪声融入掩码信号，对比研究了数字掩码（二值、六值）与模拟掩码（混沌）在不同强度噪声下TDRC的性能表现。结果表明，使用数字二值掩码的系统最高可容忍信噪比7.539 dB的强掩码噪声，其噪声容忍度远大于模拟混沌掩码（约18dB）。同时发现，掩码波形的拓扑复杂度对系统抗噪能力也有关键影响，即使在同类型掩码下，不同波形模式的系统掩码噪声容忍度最大可差10.8 dB。结合非线性动力学开展机理剖析，阐明该性能差异的内在物理成因，为未来延时型储备池计算系统的全硬件集成提供了重要指导。

title: Probability Logic Dynamic Matrix Formula
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic logic-based matrix formula designed for efficient computation and optimization, particularly within the realms of machine learning and optimization problems. The core mechanism leverages a dynamic adjustment mechanism embedded within the matrix formula itself, allowing for automatic parameter variation and model refinement. Traditional matrix approaches often require a one-time adjustment, hindering their adaptability to evolving data. This work proposes a method that dynamically adapts the matrix's parameters based on the input data, improving performance and robustness. The formula's design incorporates a layered approach that combines probabilistic reasoning with matrix operations, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Probability Density Estimation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to probability density estimation leveraging quantum entanglement. We propose a method wherein entangled particles are utilized to create a correlated probabilistic field, effectively acting as a quantum sensor. This sensor allows for the calculation of highly accurate probabilities with a dramatically reduced computational cost compared to conventional methods. The core mechanism centers around establishing a strong correlation between the entangled particles, allowing for the quantification of complex probability distributions with unparalleled precision. The resulting system offers a significant advantage in terms of efficiency and accuracy, potentially revolutionizing probabilistic modeling across various fields. The paper details the theoretical framework, experimental setup, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this quantum-enhanced approach.

abstract: This paper explores the application of topological dynamics to information theory, focusing on the development of a novel algorithmic approach for quantum information processing. This work proposes a new methodology that integrates topological principles with information theory, aiming to provide a powerful tool for the design and implementation of quantum information processing systems. The paper details the core mechanism, highlights its potential advantages, and discusses future research directions.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Classical Geometry: A Computational Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, possesses unique properties that offer the potential for transformative computational capabilities. This paper explores the application of entangled states to construct a novel computational framework, leveraging entanglement for instantaneous information transfer and synchronization. We propose a model that transforms entanglement into a geometric structure, enabling near-instantaneous data synchronization, and investigate its potential within distributed computation. The core claim centers on the realization of instantaneous data exchange and synchronization through the exploitation of entanglement's inherent properties. This work suggests a significant departure from traditional algorithmic approaches, offering a potential pathway for large-scale distributed computation with enhanced efficiency.

title: Title: Constraint-Based Graph Embedding with Implicit Regularization
abstract: The task of learning graph embeddings, which represent graph structures in a lower-dimensional space, is a fundamental challenge in many applications, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and drug discovery. Traditional graph embedding methods often rely on handcrafted features or complex optimization techniques, which can be computationally expensive and may not capture the full complexity of the graph. This paper proposes a novel constraint-based graph embedding approach that utilizes an implicit regularization scheme to dynamically adjust the strength of the regularization during the embedding process. We introduce a learning algorithm that iteratively refines the regularization parameters based on the graph's structural properties, aiming to produce embeddings that are more stable, meaningful, and generalizable. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through theoretical analysis and experimental validation, showcasing its ability to generate embeddings that effectively capture key graph characteristics.

title: Bayesian Predictive Geometry (BPG)
abstract: Abstract: Create a Bayesian framework for geometric prediction, allowing for automated discovery of hidden patterns and optimization of design through probabilistic modeling. This paper introduces Bayesian Predictive Geometry (BPG), a novel approach that integrates Bayesian inference with geometric analysis to enable the automatic discovery of hidden patterns and optimization of design parameters. We detail the core mechanism of BPG, which involves constructing a probabilistic model of a system and leveraging Bayesian techniques to predict and refine design parameters. The paper presents a comprehensive overview of the BPG framework, outlining its key components and demonstrating its effectiveness through illustrative examples. We explore the potential applications of BPG across various design domains, emphasizing its ability to uncover complex relationships and optimize design outcomes. The core claim is that BPG offers a significantly improved methodology for geometric prediction and design optimization, surpassing current point-based approaches.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Lattice Geometry (QELDG)
abstract: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Lattice Geometry (QELDG) presents a novel approach to geometric computation leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. This research investigates the potential to generate and manipulate complex geometric shapes through iterative entanglement of lattice points, creating a new class of "quantum lattices" with unprecedented control over spatial arrangement. The core mechanism focuses on implementing a system of quantum gates that progressively entangles lattice points, ultimately leading to the emergence of intricate geometric patterns. The potential of QELDG lies in its ability to represent and manipulate space in a fundamentally different way than classical methods, offering possibilities for new data representation and manipulation paradigms. This paper details the methodology, explores initial results, and discusses the implications of this approach for data science and geometric computation.

title: A Dualidade na Gestão de TI: Eficiência Operacional via IA vs. a Necessidade de Inteligência Emocional no Atendimento ao Cliente
abstract: O presente artigo analisa a dualidade contemporânea na gestão de Tecnologia da Informação (TI), contrastando a eficiência operacional promovida pela Inteligência Artificial (IA) com a demanda contínua por Inteligência Emocional (IE) no atendimento ao cliente. O objetivo central é investigar o impacto da automação na experiência do usuário (UX), identificando em quais circunstâncias o fator humano permanece insubstituível. A metodologia empregada caracteriza-se por uma pesquisa qualitativa e descritiva, fundamentada em revisão bibliográfica e na análise de métricas de desempenho, como Service Level Agreement (SLA) e Experience Level Agreement (XLA). Os resultados evidenciam que, embora a IA otimize expressivamente os tempos de resposta em operações padronizadas, ela falha em cenários que exigem alta complexidade analítica e empatia. Constatou-se que a resolutividade tecnológica decai diante da subjetividade dos problemas dos usuários. Conclui-se, portanto, que a excelência na gestão de serviços de TI exige um modelo híbrido: a IA deve atuar na escala e triagem operacional, enquanto o capital humano, munido de inteligência emocional, é direcionado estrategicamente para a resolução de conflitos, garantindo a humanização e a fidelização no suporte.

title: Growing Echo State Networks through Graph-Based Morphogenesis with Developmental Graph Cellular Automata
abstract: Developmental Graph Cellular Automata (DGCA) are a novel model of morphogenesis, capable of growing directed graphs from single-node seeds. In this paper, we extend the DGCA model to exhibit stochastic growth, and show that both deterministic and stochastic DGCAs can be trained to grow reservoirs. Reservoirs are grown with two types of targets: task-driven (using the NARMA family of tasks) and task-independent (using reservoir metrics). Results show that deterministic DGCAs are able to grow a variety of specialised, life-like structures capable of solving benchmark tasks, outperforming 'typical' reservoirs on the same task. Stochastic DGCAs grow robust, regular structures that outperform reservoirs grown deterministically. Overall, these lay the foundation for the development of DGCA systems that produce plastic reservoirs and for modelling functional, adaptive morphogenesis.

evidence.title: Growing Echo State Networks through Graph-Based Morphogenesis with Developmental Graph Cellular Automata
evidence.abstract: Developmental Graph Cellular Automata (DGCA) are a novel model of morphogenesis, capable of growing directed graphs from single-node seeds. In this paper, we extend the DGCA model to exhibit stochastic growth, and show that both deterministic and stochastic DGCAs can be trained to grow reservoirs. Reservoirs are grown with two types of targets: task-driven (using the NARMA family of tasks) and task-independent (using reservoir metrics). Results show that deterministic DGCAs are able to grow a variety of specialised, life-like structures capable of solving benchmark tasks, outperforming 'typical' reservoirs on the same task. Stochastic DGCAs grow robust, regular structures that outperform reservoirs grown deterministically. Overall, these lay the foundation for the development of DGCA systems that produce plastic reservoirs and for modelling functional, adaptive morphogenesis.

title: RegionFed: Federated Learning for Personalized Query Understanding in Heterogeneous Retail Environments
abstract: Retail search systems serve diverse geographic regions with distinct query patterns, vocabularies, and product preferences, creating significant data heterogeneity that challenges both privacy-preserving training and model personalization. Federated learning offers a natural solution for privacy, but standard FL methods produce global models that sacrifice regional performance, while existing personalized FL approaches operate at the parameter level and catastrophically collapse on modern transformers (below 10\% accuracy on T5) due to tied embeddings and LayerNorm interactions. We introduce RegionFed, an \textit{architecture-robust} federated learning framework that sidesteps this failure by operating entirely at the gradient level. RegionFed uses the $\ell_2$ conflict between regional and global gradients as a unified signal that (i) diagnoses heterogeneity, (ii) routes each region to the cheapest sufficient personalization strategy, and (iii) adaptively controls personalization strength. Because it treats models as differentiable black boxes, RegionFed deploys on T5-Small, T5-3B, RoBERTa, and CNN with zero code changes, providing large gains on transformers (where parameter-level methods collapse) and consistent improvements on CNNs. Across three public datasets (Amazon ESCI, Amazon Reviews, LEAF-FEMNIST) and four architectures, RegionFed-Meta achieves 92.27\%, closing the gap to the privacy-violating centralized upper bound (Centralized + Regional Weighting: 92.04\%, $Δ$=0.23pp, within 1$σ$) while providing $(ε{\approx}0.60)$-differential privacy and $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ convergence.

title: Learning unknown stabilizer codes using product measurements
abstract: Efficiently characterizing quantum error correcting codes is a key challenge on the path to fault-tolerant quantum computation. Stabilizer codes, a central class of such codes, are defined by a set of stabilizer generators. Here, we present an algorithm that uses random single-qubit measurements to learn the stabilizer generators of any stabilizer code from $N$ copies of stabilizer states in its codespace, requiring no prior knowledge of the code's structure. This also enables verification that a device implements its intended code. We derive a lower bound on $N$ needed to recover the stabilizer generators with high probability, together with a bound on the algorithm's overall probability of success. When applied to quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, a leading candidate for practical fault-tolerant architectures, our approach requires a number of states that scales polylogarithmically with $n$, the number of qubits.

title: Design and Development of Hybrid Learning Model for the detection of Ovarian Cancers
abstract: Ovarian cancer remains as a significant contributor to female mortality across the globe, mainly because it has a difficulty in obtaining an early and precise diagnosis through complex histopathology images. Automated image-based diagnosis has therefore become essential to assist pathologists in making effective diagnoses of malignant tissues. Traditional diagnostic procedures and Deep Learning (DL) architectures often fail to capture fine-grained cellular textures as well as global contextual relationships needed for accurate classifications. These models are based on narrow receptive fields, have no focus on critical areas, and thus, the diagnostic accuracy and generalization across subtypes are limited. In order to overcome these shortcomings, the present research proposes a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework (ViT-SE + BiGRU-Luong FusionNet) to detect ovarian cancer accurately and effectively. The Vision Transformer (ViT) with a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) module is used to learn rich global contextual dependencies and focus important feature channels adaptively. Simultaneously, the Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) with the Luong Attention mechanism accurately captures the sequential spatial dependencies and identifies critical pathological areas in tissue sequences. Finally, a Cross-Attention Fusion (CAF) module is utilised to combine complementary global and sequential representations to achieve robust classification. The proposed framework is trained and tested on the Kaggle Ovarian Cancer and Subtypes Histopathology Dataset and achieves an accuracy of 99.53%, precision of 99.41%, recall of 99.47%, specificity of 99.45% and F1-score of 99.44%. The experimental findings prove that the proposed hybrid framework substantially improves diagnostic accuracy and generalization without compromising high computational efficiency, which makes it very applicable in real-time clinical practice in medical image diagnosis.

title: 基于自适应的动态矩阵的自适应扩展
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to dynamic matrix expansion, leveraging the adaptive nature of dynamic matrices to enhance both model performance and adaptability in machine learning and data science. Traditional methods often rely on static expansions, limiting the model's flexibility. This work proposes a framework that dynamically adjusts the expansion parameters based on the input data, allowing for more efficient and robust representation learning. We detail the core mechanism of this adaptive expansion, emphasizing its impact on algorithm efficiency and generalization capabilities. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through several case studies, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and robustness compared to traditional methods. This contributes to the development of more adaptable and reliable machine learning algorithms.

title: 基于自适应量子算法的复杂系统模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for complex system simulation leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum algorithms. Traditional methods often struggle with the complexity of these systems, and this work proposes a dynamically adaptive approach to quantum simulation, aiming to enhance accuracy and speed. The core mechanism involves carefully adjusting quantum parameters through a self-optimizing algorithm, allowing for more precise simulation of intricate system dynamics. The research focuses on accelerating complex system modeling while providing accurate predictions of behavior. The paper details the framework's design, the advantages of its adaptive approach, and presents preliminary results demonstrating enhanced simulation fidelity.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子态生成算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state generation algorithm based on adaptive topology. Traditional quantum state generation methods often rely on manual design, lacking the ability for automatic learning. Our algorithm leverages the power of topological structures to efficiently generate specific quantum states, offering enhanced capabilities for quantum computing optimization and control. This approach overcomes limitations of existing techniques by providing a dynamically constructed state space that can be tailored for specific computational tasks. We present a framework for generating and manipulating quantum states utilizing adaptive topology, demonstrating its potential for significant improvements in quantum algorithm performance. The core mechanism involves constructing a topological structure that guides the creation of desired quantum states, with a focus on practical applications within quantum computing.

title: Adaptive Quantum Neural Networks: Tensor Representation Learning
abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) hold tremendous potential for revolutionizing machine learning, particularly in complex data analysis and pattern recognition. However, training QNNs can be computationally expensive and require significant expertise in network architecture and optimization. This paper proposes a novel approach to QNN training – Adaptive Tensor Representation Learning (ATRL) – which dynamically adjusts the tensor representation of the network based on the input data's unique characteristics. We demonstrate that ATRL significantly improves model performance across a range of datasets compared to traditional training methods. The method leverages the inherent properties of quantum neural networks to automatically learn and refine the tensor structure, fostering a more robust and adaptable model. This research addresses a critical bottleneck in QNN development, offering a pathway towards more efficient and effective training.

title: Title: Chaos Theory in High-Dimensional Spacetime - Predictive Modeling
abstract: Chaos Theory, a branch of mathematics dealing with complex systems exhibiting unpredictable behavior, presents a significant challenge to traditional modeling and prediction. This research delves into the application of variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) to enhance our understanding and predictive capabilities within high-dimensional spacetime. The core claim is to develop a novel framework for analyzing chaos theory within this context, generating complex dynamics and identifying critical points with unprecedented accuracy. This work proposes a quantum-enhanced approach to explore the space of possible spacetime geometries, leveraging variational quantum algorithms to create robust predictive models. The investigation focuses on the unique challenges posed by high dimensionality, and aims to overcome these limitations through a fundamentally new algorithmic strategy. This research represents a significant advancement in the field, potentially unlocking new avenues for predicting complex system behavior and advancing our comprehension of chaotic dynamics.

title: Self-Organizing Topological Structures Under Quantum Entanglement Aggregation
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource for quantum information processing, and harnessing its properties requires sophisticated techniques for manipulation and processing. This paper investigates the potential of self-organizing topological structures to facilitate efficient and stable quantum entanglement aggregation, offering a novel approach to quantum information handling. We explore the design and implementation of a quantum entanglement network based on these structures, focusing on the mechanisms that enable aggregation, splitting, and manipulation of entangled states. The core of our research lies in leveraging the inherent topological properties of these structures to create robust and controllable quantum systems. This work presents a framework for building scalable quantum entanglement networks and highlights the advantages of utilizing self-organization in achieving enhanced performance and resilience. The investigation also addresses challenges related to maintaining entanglement coherence and exploring potential applications in quantum cryptography and quantum computing.

title: Quantum Information as a Dynamic Landscape – Landscape-Based Algorithms
abstract: Quantum Information represents a fundamentally different paradigm from classical information, offering the potential for exponential speedups in computation and communication. This paper explores the application of Landscape-Based Algorithms (LBAs) to optimization problems, specifically focusing on the challenge of efficiently navigating complex search spaces. We propose a novel algorithmic approach that models the problem space as a dynamic landscape, iteratively moving across this landscape to reward solutions that are closer to the optimal solution. This framework allows for exploration of vast possibilities, dramatically improving the search efficiency compared to traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism involves a dynamic reward function that adjusts based on the landscape's characteristics, encouraging the algorithm to escape local optima and converge to a global optimum. This paper provides a detailed explanation of the Landscape model, explores its implementation, and discusses its potential impact on optimization problems across diverse domains.

title: Quantum Error Correction Codes for Distributed Storage
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum error correction (QEC) codes to enhance the reliability and security of distributed storage systems. Traditional storage methods are susceptible to various forms of data loss due to hardware failures, environmental factors, and malicious attacks. Utilizing the inherent redundancy and error-correcting capabilities of QEC codes offers a novel approach to mitigate these risks. The core claim is that leveraging QEC codes for distributed storage significantly improves its robustness. This work details a framework for implementing such a system, outlining the key mechanisms involved in data redundancy and error correction. The proposed approach represents a new paradigm in data protection, particularly relevant in scenarios demanding high data integrity, such as long-term archival and secure communication. We examine the theoretical foundations of QEC and their adaptation to the distributed storage context, emphasizing the potential for increased storage capacity and improved fault tolerance. The core mechanism relies on encoding data using QEC codes to create redundant copies, enabling the detection and correction of errors without directly observing the underlying quantum states. ---

title: Geometric Randomization for Machine Learning Model Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric randomization to enhance the optimization process in machine learning. The core concept revolves around systematically introducing variation in model parameters during each iteration, driven by random geometric transformations. We detail the methodology, its potential benefits, and preliminary results demonstrating improved model robustness and generalization. The motivation stems from the inherent challenges of optimization, particularly in complex models and datasets, where small variations can significantly impact performance. This novel technique aims to mitigate these issues by encouraging the model to explore a wider parameter space, leading to better generalization.
